title: Interleaved Pane Navigation Mesh — Prototype & Review for Console Dashboards, Rollouts, and Cost Views
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: As the Console grows to include richer dashboards, rollout controls, and token cost breakdowns, the current single-column sidebar plus global workspace switcher creates a modal-heavy flow and forces users to context-switch away from metrics when adjusting rollout policies or inspecting cost drivers. Goal: Introduce an 'Interleaved Pane Navigation Mesh' that surfaces related controls and contextual dashboards in horizontally interleaved panes rather than nested overlays, reducing cognitive load and enabling fast lateral moves between workspace state, rollout controls, and cost insights. Scope: primary flows for workspace switching, per-route rollout toggles (canary/A-B), token-level cost breakdowns, and dashboard drill-ins. This ticket covers prototype, in-team review, accessibility pass, and a small moderated usability session. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype, annotated interaction spec (Confluence), accessibility checklist, usability notes, and a follow-up eng handoff PR with acceptance criteria and visual tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates switching between workspace contexts without a blocking modal and with visible ephemeral panes for rollout and cost controls
Key routes (Dashboards / Rollouts / Cost) reachable within 2 clicks from a workspace context in prototype flows
Usability testing (n=5 product/infra engineers) median task completion <= 90s for: 'pin rollback to previous model', 'surface per-route cost spike', 'create small canary rollout'
Accessibility: keyboard focus flows for pane switching, color contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary interactive elements, screen reader labels for pane headers
Engineering handoff includes component breakdown, responsive rules (>= 1280px widescreen and 768–1279 tablet), and a proposal for progressive enhancement on mobile
design_notes: Core pattern: Interleaved panes stack horizontally and can be docked/undocked; panes are lightweight (no full-page reloads) and maintain local state when hidden
Workspace switcher becomes a top-left compact chip that opens a contextual pane rather than full screen overlay — preserves center canvas for dashboards
Rollout controls appear as a right-docked ephemeral pane when activated from a route row, with inline metric sparklines and a single-step canary slider
Cost view is a lensable pane that supports token-aggregation pivots (model, route, time window) and exposes origin links to raw request samples for debugging
Interaction heuristics: pane snoozing, ephemeral previews on hover, escape to close, and persistent breadcrumb for last active pane
Visual language: low-contrast dividers, tactile micro-interactions for pane docking (snap points), and microcopy for safe defaults (e.g., canary size suggestions)
comments: 2025-02-14 — Ava Martinez: Initial lo-fi exploration and three layout directions uploaded to Figma. Direction A (mesh with narrow panes) and Direction B (primary canvas left, stacked control panes right) recommended for studio review.

2025-02-18 — Rohan Patel: Eng feasibility check — ENG notes: dynamic panes feasible using existing layout grid; KV cache readouts may need a lightweight API endpoint for the small sparklines. Asked for API contract example.

2025-02-22 — Priya Singh (PM): PM review — prioritized cost-view drill path and tie to billing team metrics. Requested a visible CTA to 'open cost incident' that creates a ticket prefilled with selected scope.
2025-02-24 — Accessibility review request sent to D&I. Added keyboard-only prototype flows and ARIA label notes.

2025-02-27 — Usability session (moderated, 5 participants) completed. Top findings: users liked lateral movement but asked for clearer affordance for 'pinning' panes; confusion around workspace chip discoverability. Action: add tooltip and animated reveal on first-use.

2025-03-01 — Rohan Patel: Design handoff draft for components and tokens posted. ENG feedback: confirm responsive collapse behavior and the data contract for canary slider (min, max, default), and whether rollouts can be edited inline or require a dedicated dialog.
2025-03-02 — Ava Martinez: Updated Figma with pinned-state variations and added microcopy for rollout safety (rollback TTL). Moving to In Review for design + infra.

Reviewer comments: Sarah Kim (Design Lead) — looks good, minor refinement on pane header density; Marcus Lee (Infra Eng) — will schedule a spike to evaluate memory overhead of persistent pane state on low-memory instances.
decisions: Adopt interleaved pane model as experiment channel for console-ia-redesign (90-day experiment)
Keep workspace switcher as compact chip that opens contextual pane instead of full overlay
Rollout controls will use a right-docked ephemeral pane with inlined sparkline metrics and a single-step canary slider; complex edits go to a confirmation dialog
Cost view lens will expose a lightweight 'sample requests' link tied to the tracing system rather than full trace fetch in prototype
